parts.text:
{
  "extractions": [
    {
      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],
        "scope_text": "Applicable to an employee of a covered employer seeking status as an eligible employee.",
        "context_quotes": ["F000"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F001:F004",
        "references": ["§ 825.801", "§ 825.105(b)"],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has met the requirement to have been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, provided the rules in paragraph (b) are met.",
        "context_quotes": ["F002"],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F005",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the conditions in paragraph (b) are satisfied."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005", "F006"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).",
        "context_quotes": ["F005"],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": ["paragraph (b)(2)"],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F007"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where a break in service of more than seven years exists, and one of the qualifying exceptions applies.",
        "context_quotes": ["F006"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F008", "F009"],
        "choice_quote": "F007:F009",
        "choice_text": "Either (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": ["38 U.S.C. 4301"],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation (and the period of absence necessitated by such service must also be counted, without providing greater entitlement than USERRA), or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F010"],
        "scope_text": "In determining weeks of employment and whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": ["F002", "F005"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; and for determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F011"],
        "scope_text": "When an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years in determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": ["F006"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "While employers are not prevented from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "Determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.",
        "context_quotes": ["F003"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": ["paragraph (c)(2)", "§ 825.801", "29 CFR part 785"],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to FLSA principles for determining compensable hours of work based on actual hours worked; it is not limited by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements, and any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA principles may be used."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "Determining FMLA leave eligibility for an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": ["F003", "F012"],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the absence necessitated by USERRA-covered service, added to hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period, and the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F014"],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.",
        "context_quotes": ["F012"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": ["29 CFR part 541", "§ 825.102", "§ 825.801(d)"],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "Determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": ["F002", "F003"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start; if an employee is on non-FMLA leave when meeting the 12-month requirement, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason thereafter is FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "prohibition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "When an employee's leave has already started, or when an employee gives notice of the need for leave.",
        "context_quotes": ["F004"],
        "modality_quote": "may not",
        "modality": "must_not",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave; once determined eligible in response to that notice, eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in employee count within 75 miles for that specific notice, and an employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50."
      }
    }
  ]
}

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applicable to an employee of a covered employer seeking status as an eligible employee.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has met the requirement to have been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, provided the rules in paragraph (b) are met.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the conditions in paragraph (b) are satisfied.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where a break in service of more than seven years exists, and one of the qualifying exceptions applies.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation (and the period of absence necessitated by such service must also be counted, without providing greater entitlement than USERRA), or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining weeks of employment and whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; and for determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years in determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: While employers are not prevented from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to FLSA principles for determining compensable hours of work based on actual hours worked; it is not limited by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements, and any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA principles may be used.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Determining FMLA leave eligibility for an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the absence necessitated by USERRA-covered service, added to hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period, and the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start; if an employee is on non-FMLA leave when meeting the 12-month requirement, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason thereafter is FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee's leave has already started, or when an employee gives notice of the need for leave.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave; once determined eligible in response to that notice, eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in employee count within 75 miles for that specific notice, and an employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.
